ryan: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak I'm seeing tiny correctness diffs on long-context FP8 mixed-precision matmuls. Repro + perf attached below.

anya: Can you paste a minimal repro? sequence len / batch / model?

ryan: repro command: `./run_infer --model gptx-mix --dtype fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 2 --verify -o out.json`
small diff: token 10240 logprob delta ~0.078, and generated token differs at position 10241. Only reproducible when warmup KV > ~1k tokens.

mike: interesting — I saw similar once. Did we change calibration defaults? per-tensor vs per-channel? That can cause saturation in activation ranges for some heads.

ryan: we switched to fast calibration (per-tensor median) in the kernel-selector PR to reduce startup cost. PR: #1432 (sha: b3a9f2c).

julie: I ran perf profiling on canary with the change. Observed kernel switch at runtime:
```
selected_kernel: fp8_matmul_fast_v2 (fallback to fp16 if overflow)
seq_len: 4096
batch: 2
gpu_util: 72% -> 86% (after switch)
p99_latency: 220ms -> 235ms
warp_stalls: +18%
memory_bandwidth: +7%
```
Also saw occasional divergence in outputs after KV reuse.

mike: KV-pack state could be carrying scale metadata per-chunk. If we switched calibration to per-tensor but still read per-channel headers, scale mismatch could silently quantize incorrectly.

ryan: quick dump from failing run (snip):
```
KVHeader: {num_chunks: 3, scale_mode: "per-channel", scale_version: 2}
KernelScaleState: {active: per-tensor, cached_scales: [0.012,0.015,...]}
```
We were not invalidating kernel scale state when selecting fast per-tensor path -> consistent-looking but wrong ops.

anya: Oof. Does this only affect FP8 matmul path or INT8/4-bit too?

mike: likely impacts any mixed-precision path that reuses cached scale metadata. FP8 is more sensitive due to narrower range. INT8 had more conservative fallback checks.

ryan: quick patch idea — on kernel-selection change where calibration mode != cached header mode invalidate KV-scale cache for affected KV chunks. Pseudo: 
```
if (kernel.calib_mode != kv.header.scale_mode) {
  kv.invalidate_scales_for_chunks(chunks_affected);
}
```
Applied locally and re-ran 200 samples. Correctness: 200/200 matched baseline. Perf: p99 down to 195ms, throughput +6% for this workload.

julie: please add microbenchmark numbers (batch sizes 1,2,4 at seq 2048/4096) to the PR. Need before we ship. Also add a note in kernel-selector that calibration mode is tied to KV metadata.

devops: infra-bot deployed PR to canary-gpu-3 last night (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-16-09). We should run a slow rollout if tests pass.

perf-jen: I'll add a regression test to perf-suite: long-context generation with repeated prefix reuse and verify token-level equality plus logprob threshold. TODOs: add test, add kernel selector flag to force old behavior.

mike: one more thought — we should instrument a debug-only check in runtime: on reuse path, verify per-token reconstruct error < epsilon for a short sample and log if > threshold. Avoids silent corruption in prod.

ryan: agreed. I'll open follow-ups: (1) bugfix PR with KV invalidation and unit tests, (2) instrumentation PR for runtime checks, (3) perf numbers in PR description.

anya: thanks for triage. If anyone hits a repro, ping me and I can help bisect the kernel-selection heuristics.

infra-bot: deploy status: canary-gpu-3 roll started 2026-03-16T09:05Z, health: healthy -> degraded -> healthy (after rollback attempt). See /deploys/2026-03-16-09 for logs.

julie: patch LGTM after tests. Please include changelog entry under "runtime: kv-scale invalidation on kernel-calib mismatch".

devops: scheduling canary expansion tomorrow at 02:00 UTC if no regressions.

ryan: quick summary for the thread: root cause = cached KV scale metadata not invalidated when kernel calibration mode changed; triggers silent FP8 saturation/corruption on long-context reuse. Fix = invalidate scales on mismatch + add runtime debug check. Perf impact = small improvement for affected workloads after forcing right kernel.

perf-jen: adding test now, will post results within 24h. :rocket:
